label: lpullback
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
(1) Let $E:=\{\alpha<\lambda\mathrel{|}\allowbreak j(\alpha)\in S\}$.
    Suppose for contradiction that $|E|=\lambda$.
    Fix a bijection $e:\lambda\rightarrow E$.
    By elementarity, $j(e):j(\lambda)\rightarrow j(E)$ is a bijection in $M$.
    Let
    $$C:=\{\beta<j(\lambda)\mathrel{|}\allowbreak j(e)(\beta)\in S\}.$$
    Then $C\in M$. Since $j(e)$ maps $C$ injectively into $S$,
    $|C|^M\le|S|^M<d$.

    For every $\alpha<\lambda$, we have $e(\alpha)\in E$, so
    $$j(e)(j(\alpha))=j(e(\alpha))\in S.$$
    Thus $j(\alpha)\in C$, and hence $j[\lambda]\subseteq C$.
    Note also that $C\in M$ and $|C|^M<d$.
    This contradicts the minimality of $D$.

    (2) Fix in $M$ a bijection $f:D\rightarrow d$, and put $R:=f[j[\lambda]]$.
    Then $R\subseteq d$ and $|R|=\lambda$.
    If $R$ were bounded in $d$, there would be some $\gamma<d$ with $R\subseteq\gamma$.
    Then $f^{-1}[\gamma]\in M$ would contain $j[\lambda]$ and have $M$-cardinality
    $|\gamma|^M<d$, contradicting the minimality of $D$.
    Hence $R$ is cofinal in $d$.

label: lcapacity
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
we first reduce to $|T|^M<d$ and then find a set $E\subseteq j[\lambda]$ of size less than $\lambda$ that separates the members of $F\cap T$.

    By Lemma~\ref{lpullback}(2), fix a set $R\subseteq d$ cofinal in $d$ with $|R|\le\lambda$.
    Fix in $M$ an injection $q:T\rightarrow d$, and for every $r\in R$ let $T_r:=\{t\in T\mathrel{|}\allowbreak q(t)\le r\}$.
    Then $T_r\in M$ and $|T_r|^M\le|r+1|^M<d$, since $d$ is an infinite cardinal of $M$.
    By cofinality of $R$, $T=\bigcup_{r\in R}T_r$.
    Thus, if the inequality~\eqref{eq1} holds for each $T_r$,
    it also holds for $T$,
    since $|R|\leq \lambda$ and
    $\lambda\cdot 2^{<\lambda}=2^{<\lambda}$.

    We may therefore assume that $|T|^M<d$.

    \begin{claim}\label{cldelta}
        Suppose that $A,B\subseteq\lambda$ are distinct. Then
        $$\min\bigl((j(A)\cap D)\mathbin{\bigtriangleup}(j(B)\cap D)\bigr)=j\bigl(\min(A\mathbin{\bigtriangleup} B)\bigr).$$
    \end{claim}
    \begin{proof}
        Let $\delta:=\min(A\mathbin{\bigtriangleup} B)$.
        We need to prove that $\min\bigl((j(A)\cap D)\mathbin{\bigtriangleup}(j(B)\cap D)\bigr)=j(\delta)$.
        First, we have
        $$(j(A)\cap D)\mathbin{\bigtriangleup}(j(B)\cap D)=\bigl(j(A)\mathbin{\bigtriangleup} j(B)\bigr)\cap D.$$
        Second, by elementarity, $j(A)\mathbin{\bigtriangleup} j(B)=j(A\mathbin{\bigtriangleup} B)$, and its least element is $j(\delta)$.
        Since $j[\lambda]\subseteq D$, it follows that $j(\delta)\in D$ and
        hence
        $$j(\delta)= \min\bigl((j(A)\mathbin{\bigtriangleup} j(B))\cap D\bigr)= \min\bigl((j(A)\cap D)\mathbin{\bigtriangleup}(j(B)\cap D)\bigr).$$
    \end{proof}

    Let
    $S:=\{\min(X\mathbin{\bigtriangleup} Y)\mathrel{|}\allowbreak X,Y\in T\cap\mathcal P(D)^M\text{ and }X\neq Y\}$ and let $E:=j[\lambda]\cap S$.
    Since $D$ is a set of ordinals, the set $S$ is well-defined.
    Since $T\cap\mathcal P(D)^M\in M$, $S$ belongs to $M$.
    Moreover, $F\cap T\subseteq T\cap\mathcal P(D)^M$, and
    $|S|^M\le|T\times T|^M<d$.
    Since $j$ is injective and $j[\{\alpha<\lambda\mathrel{|}\allowbreak j(\alpha)\in S\}]=E$, Lemma~\ref{lpullback}(1) gives
    $$|E|=|\{\alpha<\lambda\mathrel{|}\allowbreak j(\alpha)\in S\}|<\lambda.$$

    Now define $\Phi:F\cap T\longrightarrow\mathcal P(E)$ by letting
    $\Phi(X):=X\cap E$ for every $X\in F\cap T$.
    We claim that $\Phi$ is injective.
    Take distinct $X,Y\in F\cap T$, and choose $A,B\subseteq\lambda$ such that
    $X=j(A)\cap D$ and $Y=j(B)\cap D$.
    Then $A\neq B$. Let $\delta:=\min(A\mathbin{\bigtriangleup} B)$.
    By Claim~\ref{cldelta},
    $$j(\delta)=\min(X\mathbin{\bigtriangleup} Y)\in S.$$
    Thus $j(\delta)\in j[\lambda]\cap S=E$, and $j(\delta)$ belongs to exactly one of $X$ and $Y$.
    Consequently $j(\delta)\in\Phi(X)\mathbin{\bigtriangleup}\Phi(Y)$, so $\Phi(X)\neq\Phi(Y)$.
    Therefore,
    $|F\cap T|\le|\mathcal P(E)|=2^{|E|}\le 2^{<\lambda}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
We argue by induction on the infinite cardinals $\lambda \geq \kappa$.
    Assume that $\textsf{\textup{GCH}}$ holds below $\lambda$.
    Then $2^{<\lambda}=\lambda$ and
    it suffices to prove that $2^\lambda\le (2^{<\lambda})^+$.
    Choose a definable elementary embedding $j:V\rightarrow M$ and a minimal $D\in M$ witnessing the $\lambda$-strong compactness of $\kappa$.
    Let $d:=|D|^M<j(\kappa)$.

    Since $\textsf{\textup{GCH}}$ holds below $\kappa$, elementarity gives
    $M\models$ ``$\textsf{\textup{GCH}}$ holds below $j(\kappa)$''.
    Since $d$ is an infinite cardinal of $M$ below $j(\kappa)$,
    we have $M\models|\mathcal P(D)|=d^+$.
    Let $\theta:=(d^+)^M$.
    Fix in $M$ a bijection $h:\theta\rightarrow\mathcal P(D)^M$, and put
    $$F:=\{j(A)\cap D\mathrel{|}\allowbreak A\subseteq\lambda\}.$$
    Since $j[\lambda]\subseteq D$, for every $A\subseteq\lambda$ and $\alpha<\lambda$,
    $$\alpha\in A\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad j(\alpha)\in j(A)\cap D.$$
    Thus $A\mapsto j(A)\cap D$ is injective, and $|F|=2^\lambda$.

    For every $\beta<\theta$, we have $h[\beta]\in M$ and $|h[\beta]|^M\le d$, because $\theta=(d^+)^M$.
    Now applied Lemma~\ref{lcapacity} to $T:=h[\beta]$, therefore gives
    $$|F\cap h[\beta]|\le 2^{<\lambda}.$$
    Hence $2^\lambda=|F|=|F\cap h[\theta]|\le (2^{<\lambda})^+$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The same argument applies locally:
    if $\kappa\le \lambda$ are two uncountable cardinals and $\kappa$ is $\lambda$-strongly compact and $\textsf{\textup{GCH}}$ holds below $\kappa$,
    then $2^\mu=\mu^+$ for every infinite cardinal $\mu\le\lambda$,
    since $\lambda$-strong compactness implies $\mu$-strong compactness whenever $\kappa\le\mu\le\lambda$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
The proofs above don't use $\operatorname{crit}(j)=\kappa$.
    If $\kappa$ is $\omega_1$-strongly compact (in the sense of Definition~\ref{dfine}, with
    $\operatorname{crit}(j)\ge\omega_1$ in place of $\operatorname{crit}(j)=\kappa$), the same proofs apply.
    Consequently, if $\kappa$ is $\omega_1$-strongly compact and $\textsf{\textup{GCH}}$ holds below $\kappa$, then $\textsf{\textup{GCH}}$ holds.
head: environment
